entries.description: All-domains DNS token used by the pinned CLI, hosting helper, and hosted MCP.
permissions: Zone: DNS Edit for all zones
Zone: Zone Read for all zones
notes: Provider label: Agent DNS — all domains. Scope was user-authorized and verified on 2026-10-14; use check --live to establish current access.
The profile is ignored, owner-only mode 600, in an owner-only mode-700 directory. No token value belongs in this inventory.
The profile also contains the non-secret account selector. The default zone is deliberately unbound; project manifests choose their zone.

Permissions are the dashboard-confirmed declared grant. Read-only checks prove token/user/zone/DNS reads, not DNS Edit or all-zone grants. The deprecated zone.permissions field is not API-token introspection.

entries.description: Explicit Railway workspace profile for WebArts and Paul.
permissions: Existing workspace access; do not infer scope from account identity endpoint failures
notes: The existing profile remains outside this repository. It is owner-only mode 600. Inventory records its location; this task does not migrate or rotate it.

entries.description: Legacy shell credential source for another Railway workspace.
notes: Reference only. This shell script may contain other credentials or commands; inventory checks do not read or source it. Never substitute its token for the explicitly selected workspace profile.

This is also the global shell secret source. App-local .env files use their own loaders; see environment.project-secrets and the customization runbook. Authorized edits must preserve unrelated assignments and avoid printing values.

entries.description: Cloudflare authentication and target selector variable names.
notes: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is secret. Account/zone IDs are non-secret selectors.

Pinned CLI and MCP wrappers load the credential profile over inherited variables. Hosting API uses manifest account/zone selectors before profile selectors. CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID is optional and absent from the current all-domains profile.
If a zone selector is absent from the profile, an inherited CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID can still be a fallback. Inspect or unset it when switching project context.

entries.description: Railway workspace credentials, CI credentials, and target selectors.
notes: RAILWAY_API_TOKEN and RAILWAY_TOKEN are secret. IDs and branch names are selectors.

Workspace launchers clear inherited Railway tokens before loading the selected profile. RAILWAY_TOKEN is project/environment CI access; its value is maintained in the relevant CI secret store, not this registry.

notes: The installer owns model, model_reasoning_effort, model_verbosity, model_reasoning_summary, web_search, and service_tier when present in this file.

Captured from the current machine without changing their values. Other preferences, host paths, and application state remain in the ignored active config. Project config and runtime overrides can take precedence.

entries.description: Official hosted Cloudflare MCP with token-backed internal auth.
notes: The header helper emits credentials to the application auth pipe. Never invoke it to display or log its output.
Codex uses the owner-only profile through the header helper. Cursor has its own OAuth connection state and may require sign-in. A URL alone is not authenticated access.

entries.description: Official native Railway MCP using an explicit workspace profile.
notes: bin/railway-mcp selects the WebArts profile by default; another workspace requires an explicit profile.

entries.description: Pinned official cf CLI with explicit local credential loading.
notes: Restore from the lockfile with npm ci --prefix ~/.agents/tools --ignore-scripts. Preserve existing Wrangler workflows.

entries.description: Existing native Railway CLI used by project and MCP operations.
notes: Installed outside this repository. Use railway --version to check the installed version. Project repositories own their CLI and SDK pins; this inventory does not update them.

entries.description: Paul Railway environments, source branches, domains, and credential-profile references.
notes: The Paul manifest owns stable IDs and main/dev versus prod/production mappings. scripts/hosting.py validates those identities before DNS work. A broad credential does not authorize unrelated mutations.

entries.description: Agent utility PATH setup without global secret injection.
notes: The shell hook adds ~/.agents/bin. Existing terminals can source config/env.sh; desktop processes may need explicit absolute utility paths.

entries.description: All local skill entrypoints, imported skill provenance, and adaptations.
notes: docs/INVENTORY.md derives every skills/*/SKILL.md entrypoint. Imported provider revisions and local adaptations come from config/skill-sources.json; local skills use Git history.

entries.description: Tracked helper scripts and executable wrappers.
notes: The generated inventory derives bin/* and scripts/* files. Inspect purpose and side effects before executing a helper; lookup never executes commands declared in metadata.

entries.description: Version-controlled global agent context and maintenance rules.
notes: Persistent customization tasks must update inventory references, runbooks, and meaningful change history in the same PR.
AGENTS.md is the concise repository entrypoint. rules/AGENTS.md supplies the broader global instructions linked into Codex.

entries.description: Codex-managed sign-in and credential storage.
notes: Credential storage is controlled by the active cli_auth_credentials_store setting. Codex may use its native auth file or OS credential store.
Use codex login status to inspect sign-in and the supported login flow to restore it. Do not copy auth data into shared config. Local inventory checks do not read auth storage.

entries.description: Application-managed MCP runtimes alongside the two shared provider definitions.
notes: Registered application-owned runtimes: node_repl and computer-use. Their executable paths and lifecycle remain application-managed; checks flag unregistered runtimes without displaying their configuration.

entries.description: Registered plugin enablement, managed through Codex application settings.
notes: Enablement snapshot registered on 2026-10-14. It is not an installer input; checks flag added, removed, or changed plugin toggles without displaying application config.
Plugin caches, OAuth grants, hooks, and runtime state remain application-owned. Inventory documents the customization and update location, not credential contents.

entries.description: Ignored installer backups, plans, journals, verification reports, and screenshots.
notes: Installer backups can contain credentials or private application settings. Keep them ignored and owner-only; backup references and recovery steps live in the runbooks.
local/inventory/status.json is a sanitized observation, not durable proof of current provider access. Git does not back up secret values; keep an encrypted backup or a replacement procedure.

entries.description: Customization metadata index, schema, generated documentation, and change history.
notes: Edit registered metadata in config/inventory.json; existing manifests own settings and locations. Run agents-config docs to regenerate the Markdown view.
The schema forbids secret-value fields. Local verification results remain ignored observations; meaningful changes belong in CHANGELOG.md and Git/PR history.

entries.description: Single source of credential profile IDs and file locations for wrappers, hosting, and inventory.
notes: Profile IDs such as cloudflare.default and railway.webarts resolve through this catalog. Hosting manifests select IDs; explicit file paths remain supported for ad hoc profiles. Do not put values in the catalog.

entries.description: Pinned, hash-verified TOML editor for preserving application configuration.
notes: Restore with the README pip command into ignored local/python-packages. No global Python packages are changed. Inventory metadata lookup and generation remain standard-library operations; configuration rendering uses the pinned editor.

entries.description: GitHub CLI authentication and separate agent-connector account state.
notes: GitHub CLI uses its native credential store and configuration under ~/.config/gh. Do not copy credentials into this repository. Select the intended repository owner/host explicitly.
Use gh api user --jq .login to confirm the CLI account without printing tokens. Agent GitHub connectors have their own selected connection; CLI authentication does not establish connector identity.
Change sign-in through supported gh auth login/account selection or the connector settings within the current task authorization. Inventory does not inspect native credential values.

entries.description: Codex/Cursor native discovery research, capability gaps, and proposed lifecycle improvements.
notes: The plan distinguishes documented conventions, dated local observations, and work not yet applied. The maintenance skill is portable; native hooks, roles, execution policies, and application-owned tools need client-specific adapters.

entries.description: Native Codex execution rules and application-owned sandbox/approval policy.
notes: The native rule file exists and is not copied into this public repository. It contains executable command-prefix policy, not Markdown instructions.

Current policy observations are dated in docs/agent-harnesses.md. Inventory checks do not parse or verify effective execution rules, project overrides, managed requirements, or hook trust. Preserve native state until a task requests a policy change.

entries.description: Cursor agent CLI preferences and command/file/MCP permission entries.
notes: This file is native JSON and is not managed by the shared installer. Project permission overrides use .cursor/cli.json. It is distinct from editor permissions.json and sandbox.json.

The file exists, but no agent/cursor-agent executable was found on the inspected shell PATH. The cursor executable opens the editor. Check current installation and effective configuration before relying on CLI behavior.

entries.description: Cursor account/user rules and project instruction entrypoints.
notes: User Rules are maintained through Customize -> Rules. No shared global startup bridge is registered or verified yet; see the implementation plan.

Repository AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/*.mdc are project conventions. Do not infer that ~/.agents/AGENTS.md or ~/.codex/AGENTS.md supplies global Cursor instructions. Preserve existing User/Team Rules and verify fresh-session context.

entries.description: Cursor editor settings and separate optional native sandbox/Auto-review files.
notes: Keep the full native file and account state application-owned; export only deliberately managed preference keys.

Optional ~/.cursor/sandbox.json and ~/.cursor/permissions.json have different roles and schemas. Their absence does not determine effective UI/team policy. These surfaces are documented, not fully checked by agents-config.

entries.description: Cursor-managed account sign-in and per-client MCP authentication.
notes: Use supported Cursor account/MCP settings for sign-in and recovery. Native OAuth/credentials remain private and are not read by inventory checks.
The shared MCP JSON defines connections; a successful Codex/CLI connection does not establish authentication or available tools in Cursor. Verify each client against its intended account/resource.

entries.description: Application-local environment files and their runtime loaders.
notes: Each project owns its .env, .env.local, or other declared environment-file locations and loader precedence. Inspect applicable project documentation and code; no global .env discovery or automatic loading by both agents is assumed.

The existing railway.legacy-profile entry records ~/.secrets.sh; config/profiles.json owns registered provider-profile locations. Add per-project references and secret variable names when onboarding an app, never values, fragments, or hashes.

The user intends agents to make authorized environment/secret edits. Filesystem sandbox access, provider permission, and reload/redeploy behavior still need explicit capability checks in the selected harness.

entries.description: Existing local application/service ownership and lifecycle commands.
notes: This external workspace document points to ~/git/local-dev/README.md and its service registry. It remains owned by those repositories; do not duplicate ports, routes, or process state here.
Use the owning manager and verify live PID/CWD/ownership/readiness before start/stop/kill. This registry entry is context, not a live service-health check.
